results.program_or_pathway: Georgian National Film Centre Production Incentive
results.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
results.authoritative_rule_set: Film in Georgia is a 20% cash rebate on qualified expenditure incurred in Georgia, with a further 2%-5% cultural uplift after the base certificate. A Georgia-registered production entity applies; at least 50% of the production budget must be mobilized at application; the applicant contracts with Enterprise Georgia, completes the production, and submits an independent qualified-cost audit within one year of certification. The official programme page sets five one-point uplift criteria covering release/making-of, specified Georgian key personnel, Georgian cultural content, at least GEL50,000 Georgian post-production, and qualifying international distribution or festival recognition. Local-entity payment alone does not qualify non-Georgian expenditure.

authority_sources.title: Enterprise Georgia — Film in Georgia
authority_sources.pinpoint: 20% base, Georgia entity, 50% finance gate, audit/payment process and 2%-5% cultural uplift criteria

authority_sources.title: Enterprise Georgia — Film in Georgia official brochure
authority_sources.pinpoint: qualified expenditure guidance and programme process

results.optimizer_consequence: Model 20% base only after Georgian-incurrence and applicant/preapproval gates; treat the additional 2%-5% as separately earned cultural points, not an automatic 25%.

results.program_or_pathway: Turkey Cinema General Directorate Production Support
results.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
results.authoritative_rule_set: Foreign Film Production Support is selective support of up to 30% of the accepted amount spent in Turkey. The foreign producer must contract with an eligible Turkish co-producer or service company, which applies; the Turkish applicant must satisfy the official recent-production/service track record. The project must score at least 50/100 on the qualification test, be commercially exhibited abroad, and meet current minimum Turkey expenditure of TRY30 million for a feature, TRY6 million for a documentary, or TRY10 million per series episode. For co-productions, eligible Turkey expenditure is apportioned by the foreign producer's ownership share. Payment is made once after completion on invoices and a sworn CPA report. The support cannot be combined with co-production support.

authority_sources.pinpoint: foreign-production permit and Turkish host requirement

results.optimizer_consequence: Use a conditional maximum 30% on accepted Turkey expenditure with the current format threshold, local applicant, 50-point, approval/audit and non-stacking gates; do not treat payer location alone as qualification.

results.starting_issue: Reconcile current treaties/MOUs, formats, contribution tests, approval timing and national-treatment consequences.
results.authoritative_rule_set: Screen Australia's current list contains 12 treaty partners and two MOU partners. Official status requires an applicable arrangement, independent co-producers, matching financial and creative participation, nationality/personnel and territorial compliance, provisional applications before pre-production, and joint competent-authority approval. Arrangement-specific format rules control. Official status treats the work as Australian and can bypass the Significant Australian Content test for Producer Offset eligibility, but neither certification nor funding is automatic.

results.effective_date: Current partner list checked 2026-08-11; guidelines dated 2023
results.optimizer_consequence: Generate an official co-production pathway only for a listed arrangement and its format-specific terms; domestic Producer Offset/QAPE rules remain separate eligibility calculations.
results.instrument: Treaties with Canada, China, Germany, India, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa and the United Kingdom; MOUs with France and New Zealand.
results.version: Current Screen Australia partner list and arrangement texts as at 2026-08-11
results.contribution_rules: Minimum 30% for Canada, Italy and UK; 20% for China, India, Ireland, Israel, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore and South Africa; Germany 30%, reducible to 20% exceptionally or for multipartite projects; New Zealand has no stated treaty minimum but Screen Australia expects 20%; France requires at least 40% Australian and 20% French. Financial and creative participation must be reasonably proportional.
results.national_treatment: Jointly approved productions are national productions in each party; in Australia they may access Producer Offset without the Significant Australian Content test and may apply for public funding, subject to every separate program rule.
results.competent_authorities: Screen Australia for Australia and the competent authority named by each partner arrangement; all relevant authorities must jointly approve.
results.domestic_incentive_interaction: Official status is a qualification route, not an incentive award. Producer Offset certification, QAPE, thresholds and other domestic funding requirements remain independently applicable.

results.starting_issue: Diff complete current Telefilm treaty/MOU list; capture texts, authorities, contribution and nationality rules.
results.authoritative_rule_set: Telefilm's current official directory displays 57 country/territory headings, with the Belgium heading covering the Flemish, French and German-speaking Communities; Canadian Heritage reports 59 partner countries. Each pathway is governed by its own treaty/MOU. Telefilm requires a Canadian-controlled production company, preliminary recommendation normally at least 30 days before shooting (60 days for Hungary, Poland, Switzerland or Hong Kong), joint authority recognition, and arrangement-specific financial, creative, technical, nationality, format and territorial compliance. Contributions range from 15%-30% under the applicable treaty; participation and expenditure must be proportional. Treaty status gives national status, but CPTC and other incentives require separate applications and their remaining requirements.

results.national_treatment: Recognition by all designated authorities grants national-production status. It permits access to Canadian benefits but does not itself award a tax credit or fund.

results.domestic_incentive_interaction: For CPTC, the Canadian producer must apply separately to Telefilm and CAVCO and satisfy all remaining Act/Regulations requirements. Other federal/provincial incentives and funds retain separate eligibility and expense rules.
